files.description: Repo commands, existing test setup and default PR evidence

rules.rule: Our engineering best practices live in the Paella-Labs/best-practices repository, which is available to you as cross-repo context; every Markdown file in it applies. Repo-specific commands, test setup and default PR evidence are in this repo's AGENTS.md. Both the PR changes and your review comments must comply with them. Do not flag pre-existing violations in surrounding code outside the scope of the change, since we favor incremental improvement over broad consistency enforcement. When flagging a violation, cite the specific file and rule so engineers understand the rationale and can propose upstream changes if they disagree.

Customer protection is the TOP priority in every review. Flag testing gaps at all levels (e.g. unit, e2e) where critical assumptions introduced or changed by this PR are unprotected before commenting on style or production implementation. For each gap found, suggest the highest priority minimal concrete tests that would prove the underlying assumptions are correct. The goal is not to increase trivial coverage percentage via tests that merely verify routing logic (e.g. asserting that a mocked input is returned unchanged) but to create tests that would fail if the logic were subtly wrong -- testing edge cases, error paths, and real behavioral contracts. For new or changed behavior in this PR, apply code/test.md and code/pull-requests.md from Paella-Labs/best-practices and flag: (1) a PR description with no evidence of the feature working -- the PR evidence defined in code/pull-requests.md, with this repo's default named in the Testing section of AGENTS.md, that lets a reviewer confirm the feature works without re-running anything; a pass/fail result, 'tests pass locally', a terminal screenshot or a green CI badge is not evidence; (2) tests written after the code -- where code/test.md says a test is warranted, production code whose covering tests only arrive in a later commit of the PR; (3) new or changed behavior that earns a test under code/test.md (trivial mappings, pass-through logic and logging usually don't) but that no committed test covers at any level -- ask for a test in the layer of the testing fabric that would catch a regression soonest; (4) new committed tests that do not follow the test setup (framework, file naming, location, tags, run commands) described in this repo's AGENTS.md, unless the PR explains the deviation. Apply this to the changes in this PR only: never flag pre-existing untested code or missing evidence for earlier work, since we favor incremental improvement over retroactive enforcement.
